- Implemented functionality to upsert billing data from Stripe invoices, payments, and subscriptions, ensuring accurate mirroring of Stripe data in the local database.

- Updated the `BillingModule` to integrate the new services and streamline the billing workflow.

Document the single-project, service-scoped release model.
Each backend service uploads source maps for the exact artifact it deploys.

diff --git a/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-sentry-multi-service-source-maps-design.md b/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-30-sentry-multi-service-source-maps-design.md

@@ -0,0 +1,216 @@
+# Sentry Multi-Service Source Maps Design
+
+## Summary
+
+Connexus should use one Sentry project for backend services and publish one Sentry release per service per commit. This keeps the Sentry setup simple while preventing source map collisions between the NestJS apps in the monorepo.
+
+Release format:
+
+```text
+{service}@{githubSha}
+```
+
+Examples:
+
+```text
+connexus-be@8973771ca...
+notifications@8973771ca...
+schedulers@8973771ca...
+```
+
+## Goals
+
+- Keep one backend Sentry project and one runtime `SENTRY_DSN`.
+- Make stack traces resolve correctly for each deployed service.
+- Avoid release/source-map collisions when services deploy from the same commit.
+- Preserve service, environment, and release filters in Sentry.
+- Support cron monitor check-ins for scheduler jobs.
+
+## Non-Goals
+
+- Creating one Sentry project per service.
+- Uploading frontend/browser source maps.
+- Keeping `.map` files inside runtime Docker images.
+
+## Project Model
+
+Use one Sentry project:
+
+```text
+connexus-web-api
+```
+
+All backend services report to that project. Events are separated by tags and release metadata:
+
+```text
+service = connexu

+# E-Sign Consent and Disclosure Text — Design Spec
+
+**Date:** 2026-03-12
+**Branch:** cx-esign
+**Status:** Approved
+
+---
+
+## Problem
+
+The e-sign signing flow currently accepts a single `consentText` string from the frontend during signing, but:
+
+- No canonical consent or disclosure text is stored on `SignedRecord`.
+- The view endpoint does not return any legal text to the frontend.
+- The signing endpoint does not validate that the text sent by the frontend matches anything stored on the backend.
+- `ElectronicConsent` stores a `disclosureHash` instead of the full plain-text disclosure.
+
+This makes the legal audit trail incomplete and leaves the frontend responsible for generating legal copy, which is wrong.
+
+---
+
+## Goals
+
+1. Store canonical `consentText` and `disclosureText` on each `SignedRecord` at creation time.
+2. Return both texts from the view endpoint so the frontend can render them directly.
+3. Require the frontend to echo both texts back when signing.
+4. Validate on the backend that the echoed values exactly match what is stored on the record — reject with `BadRequestException` if they do not.
+5. Persist both accepted plain-t

+# E-Sign Consent and Disclosure Text — Design Spec
+
+**Date:** 2026-03-12
+**Branch:** cx-esign
+**Status:** Approved
+
+---
+
+## Problem
+
+The e-sign signing flow currently accepts a single `consentText` string from the frontend during signing, but:
+
+- No canonical consent or disclosure text is stored on `SignedRecord`.
+- The view endpoint does not return any legal text to the frontend.
+- The signing endpoint does not validate that the text sent by the frontend matches anything stored on the backend.
+- `ElectronicConsent` stores a `disclosureHash` instead of the full plain-text disclosure.
+
+This makes the legal audit trail incomplete and leaves the frontend responsible for generating legal copy, which is wrong.
+
+---
+
+## Goals
+
+1. Store canonical `consentText` and `disclosureText` on each `SignedRecord` at creation time.
+2. Return both texts from the view endpoint so the frontend can render them directly.
+3. Require the frontend to echo both texts back when signing.
+4. Validate on the backend that the echoed values exactly match what is stored on the record — reject with `BadRequestException` if they do not.

diff:
diff --git a/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-11-esign-view-and-sign-apis-design.md b/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-11-esign-view-and-sign-apis-design.md

@@ -0,0 +1,391 @@
+# E-Sign View & Sign APIs Design
+
+## Context
+
+The e-sign module already supports creating signed records with signers and sending sequential email invitations containing JWT tokens. We need two new APIs that signers access via those token links: one to **view** the document and one to **sign** it.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- **View API**: Validate the JWT token from the email link, resolve the current version of the document, return it to the signer.
+- **Sign API**: Validate the JWT token, accept custom field data, render it into the HTML document using Handlebars, record the signature event and electronic consent, then automatically advance to the next signer or mark the record as completed.
+- All requests are authenticated solely via the JWT token (no session, no logged-in user).
+- Full audit trail at every step with tamper-evident hash chain.
+- TDD approach: tests written before implementation.
+
+## Decisions
+
+| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|
+| Architecture | Modular services + NestJS Guard | Each service <200 lines, single responsibility, guard handles token declaratively |
+| Token validation | JWT helper (pure function) + service (DB validation)
... [truncated]

+# E-Sign View & Sign APIs Design
+
+## Context
+
+The e-sign module already supports creating signed records with signers and sending sequential email invitations containing JWT tokens. We need two new APIs that signers access via those token links: one to **view** the document and one to **sign** it.
+
+## Requirements
+
+- **View API**: Validate the JWT token from the email link, resolve the current version of the document, return it to the signer.
+- **Sign API**: Validate the JWT token, accept custom field data, render it into the HTML document using Handlebars, record the signature event and electronic consent, then automatically advance to the next signer or mark the record as completed.
+- All requests are authenticated solely via the JWT token (no session, no logged-in user).
+- Full audit trail at every step with tamper-evident hash chain.
+- TDD approach: tests written before implementation.
+
+## Decisions
+
+| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|
+| Architecture | Modular services + NestJS Guard | Each service <200 lines, single responsibility, guard handles token declaratively |
+| Token validation | JWT helper (pure function) + service (DB validation)

@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+# Scheduler Scripts
+
+Standalone scripts for manually triggering scheduler jobs outside the cron cycle.
+
+## Insurance Expiry Jobs
+
+Runs all insurance policy expiry-related jobs sequentially:
+
+1. **15-Day Expiry Reminders** — Sends notifications for policies expiring in 15 days
+2. **Mark Expiring Policies** — Sets status to `EXPIRING` for policies expiring in 30 days
+3. **Mark Expired Policies** — Sets status to `EXPIRED` for policies past their expiry date
+4. **Mark Deficient Policies** — Sets `NON_COMPLIANT` expired policies to `DEFICIENT`
+
+### Usage
+
+```bash

codeText:
Subject: docs: add README for scheduler scripts, detailing insurance expiry jobs, usage, and exit codes
Body: 

Changes:
+# Scheduler Scripts
+
+Standalone scripts for manually triggering scheduler jobs outside the cron cycle.
+
+## Insurance Expiry Jobs
+
+Runs all insurance policy expiry-related jobs sequentially:
+
+1. **15-Day Expiry Reminders** — Sends notifications for policies expiring in 15 days
+2. **Mark Expiring Policies** — Sets status to `EXPIRING` for policies expiring in 30 days
+3. **Mark Expired Policies** — Sets status to `EXPIRED` for policies past their expiry date
+4. **Mark Deficient Policies** — Sets `NON_COMPLIANT` expired policies to `DEFICIENT`
+
+### Usage
+
+```bash
+npx ts-node --transpile-only -r tsconfig-paths/register apps/schedulers/src/scripts/run-insurance-expiry-jobs.ts
+```
+
+> **Note:** The `--transpile-only` flag is required to skip type-checking at runtime. Type safety is enforced by the IDE and the NestJS build pipeline.
+
+### How It Works
+
+The script bootstraps a standalone NestJS application context using `SchedulersModule`, resolves `InsuranceExpiryService`, and runs each job in sequence. Notifications are dispatched via SQS to the notification dispatcher queue. Policies are processed in batches of 100 using cursor-based pagination.

+

+

 +# E-Sign: Pre-Generate PDF Snapshots via Queue
 +
 +## Overview
 +
 +Replace on-demand HTML-to-PDF conversion in the e-sign signed-record download flow with pre-generated immutable PDF snapshots.
 +
 +For HTML-based e-sign documents:
 +
 +- generate an immutable PDF for the initial document snapshot
 +- generate an immutable PDF for every signature-event snapshot
 +- queue PDF generation asynchronously via SQS
 +- store PDF artifact state in `metaData` on the owning row
 +- stop falling back to on-demand conversion during reads
 +
 +Native PDF source documents keep the existing direct-PDF behavior and do not use this snapshot pipeline.
 +
 +## Design Decisions
 +
 +| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
 +|---|---|---|
 +| Trigger point | When immutable HTML snapshot is written | PDF should be derived from the persisted source snapshot, not generated on read |
 +| Queue transport | SQS | Reuses the repository's existing background-jobs infrastructure |
 +| Infra management | CDK-managed dedicated queue + DLQ | Keeps queue provisioning versioned and environment-aware |
 +| Reliability model | Direct SQS send after commit + SQS-native retries | SQS redrive handles retri

- Discussed current and proposed approaches for handling updates, including the use of `findMany` and `updateMany`.
- Highlighted issues with using `updateMany` for differentiated updates and provided alternative strategies for batch processing.
- Included a detailed decision-making process for selecting the optimal approach for handling readiness status updates.

+# Bulk Update Optimization Analysis
+
+## Context
+
+Analyzing the `Promise.all` block in `vendor-property-responses.service.ts` (lines 401–531) for potential optimization using `findMany` + `updateMany` instead of individual `findFirst` + `update` calls per record.
+
+---
+
+## Current Approach
+
+```typescript
+await Promise.all(
+  updateBatches[i].map(async (update) => {
+    const existingResponse = await tx.vendorPropertyResponses.findFirst({ ... });
+    // validate
+    await tx.vendorPropertyResponses.update({ ... });
+  })
+);
+```
+
+- **N `findFirst` queries** per batch (one per record)
+- **N `update` queries** per batch (one per record)
+- All run concurrently via `Promise.all`
+
+---
+
+## Proposed Idea
+
+1. Use `findMany` with mapped `updateBatches.vendorPropertyResponseId` — single read query
+2. Loop over results and build `updateData` for each
+3. Use `updateMany` to write all updates at once
+
+---
+
+## Issues with Pure `findMany` + `updateMany`
+
+### Issue 1: Each record gets DIFFERENT update data
+
+`updateMany` in Prisma applies **the same `data` payload to all matched records**. But in this logic, each record gets different values:
+
+- Record A might get `totalCost: 5000`, `vendorComments: "abc"`
+- Record B might get `upfront

+
+**Date:** 2026-02-24
+**Branch:** ms-auth-flow
+**Status:** Approved
+
+## Goal
+
+Add Microsoft login as an alternative authentication method for existing users. FE handles Microsoft auth via MSAL.js, BE verifies the token and bridges to Cognito via a Custom Auth Challenge flow, so Amplify works natively on the FE.
+
+## Constraints
+
+- Existing users only — no new user signup through Microsoft
+- Must not break the existing email/password login flow
+- FE uses Amplify with Cognito — must work natively with `signIn()`, `fetchAuthSession()`, token refresh
+- Microsoft is NOT a Cognito federated identity provider — it's handled raw by the FE
+- Minimal Lambda footprint

subject: feat: add observability, logging, and trace/log correlation stack
body:
Roll out structured logging (Winston + CloudWatch + S3 daily archive),
OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics via a self-hosted collector exporting to
AWS X-Ray and CloudWatch, Sentry cron monitoring, and end-to-end
correlationId/traceparent propagation across HTTP, SQS, and EventBridge
workers so logs, traces, and queue messages all line up.

- Adds RequestContextStorage (AsyncLocalStorage) plus a shared
  WorkerObservabilityService that wraps SQS/cron handlers in OTEL spans
  and Sentry check-ins, stamps logs with correlationId/requestId/traceId,
  and creates a fresh local requestId per consumer attempt.
- Publishes correlationId and W3C traceparent/baggage as SQS message
  attributes from every producer (shared SqsService and direct
  @ssut/nestjs-sqs handlers via a new sendWithSqsObservability helper),
  and extracts them on the consumer side so producer/consumer logs
  share a trace.
- Instruments contract, insurance, signing reminder, export, RFP mail,
  and notification listeners; aggregates partial failures in
  contract/insurance expiry crons so observeCronJob reports failure to
  Sentry instead of silently swallowing sub-step errors.
- Sanitizes shared SQS publisher debug logs to drop full message bodies
  and replaces verbose raw-body logging in the RFP mail listener with
  structured events.
- Adds the logger-infra scaffold (OTEL collector config, docker-compose,
  install script, env example), wires CI/workflow env vars, and ships
  observability docs (README, runbooks, setup checklist, metrics/alerts,
  EventBridge cron monitoring) plus the design spec and plan for trace/
  log correlation.

+

+

+  - Persisted `reminderCount` field

 +# E-Sign: Pre-Generate PDF Snapshots via Queue
 +
 +## Overview
 +
 +Replace on-demand HTML-to-PDF conversion in the e-sign signed-record download flow with pre-generated immutable PDF snapshots.
 +
 +For HTML-based e-sign documents:
 +
 +- generate an immutable PDF for the initial document snapshot
 +- generate an immutable PDF for every signature-event snapshot
 +- queue PDF generation asynchronously via SQS
 +- store PDF artifact state in `metaData` on the owning row
 +- stop falling back to on-demand conversion during reads
 +
 +Native PDF source documents keep the existing direct-PDF behavior and do not use this snapshot pipeline.
 +
 +## Design Decisions
 +
 +| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
 +|---|---|---|
 +| Trigger point | When immutable HTML snapshot is written | PDF should be derived from the persisted source snapshot, not generated on read |
 +| Queue transport | SQS | Reuses the repository's existing background-jobs infrastructure |
 +| Infra management | CDK-managed dedicated queue + DLQ | Keeps queue provisioning versioned and environment-aware |
 +| Reliability model | Direct SQS send after commit + SQS-native retries | SQS redrive handles retri

+

+

+

+
+### 1.1 Old Data Model (`sample-extracted-data-complete.json`)
+
+A **flat structure** — one document produces one set of fields, creating exactly **one InsurancePolicy**.
+
+```
+Top-level fields:
+├── policyNumber          → InsurancePolicy.policyNumber
+├── policyType            → InsurancePolicy.policyTypeCoverage (enum mapping)
+├── policyEndDate         → InsurancePolicy.policyExp
+├── policyDeductibles     → InsurancePolicy.deductables (array of arrays of {amount, type, applicableToCoverages})

+# Cancel Award Guard and Draft Contract Cleanup — Design
+
+Date: 2026-04-22
+Status: Approved (pending spec review)
+Related app: `apps/sow-rfq` (bid-review) + `apps/e-sign` data (read/write) + `libs/shared`
+
+## Problem
+
+Today, `POST bid-review/cancel-award` and `POST bid-review/cancel-award-vendor-all-properties` in `apps/sow-rfq` only revert statuses on `VendorPropertyResponses` / `RfpProperties` via status history. They do not consider the e-sign side at all.
+
+Two bugs follow from this:
+
+1. An award can be cancelled even after a contract template has been sent for signature (`Template.templateStatus = SENT`, and a `SignedRecord` graph has been created). Product wants this disallowed.
+2. When an award is cancelled while a draft `Template` exists (created but not yet sent for signature), that `Template` is left behind. Re-awarding the same property later leaves stale draft data around and can create ambiguity about which template to use. Product wants cleanup to be safe so the same property can be re-awarded and its contract regenerated from scratch.

+## Goals

+# E-Sign: Signer Copy Delivery via Pre-Signed S3 URL
+
+## Overview
+
+Add a direct PDF download link to e-sign notification emails so signers can retain a copy of their signed document without needing platform authentication.
+
+Currently, `CONTRACT_SIGNATURE_RECEIVED` and `CONTRACT_FULLY_SIGNED` emails include a frontend view link that requires platform login. External signers (consumers) may not have platform accounts, making the link inaccessible. This is a gap under ESIGN Act §101(c) which requires consumers be able to retain electronic records.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- **PDF snapshot pipeline** from the `2026-04-02-esign-pdf-snapshot-queue-design` spec must be implemented. Specifically, `PdfSnapshotMetaDataSchema` and related helpers must exist in `libs/shared/src/pdf-snapshot/`. Without this, HTML document PDF resolution has no snapshot to reference.
+
+## Design Decisions
+
+| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|
+| URL type | Pre-signed S3 URL from immutable bucket | Direct download, no authentication required, time-limited |
+| URL expiry | 7 days (604800 seconds) | Maximum S3 pre-signed URL duration; standard industry practice |
+| Document format

@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+# E-Sign PDF Placeholder Replacement
+
+**Date:** 2026-03-24
+**Status:** Approved
+
+## Problem
+
+When generating PDFs from signed record HTML, unfilled signer fields render as raw Handlebars IDs (e.g., `{{79c306e8-bad4-4925-865d-3d12dde3c278_signature_ur1uy}}`). These are ugly and meaningless to end users.
+
+## Solution
+
+Replace unfilled signer field placeholders with styled, colour-coded HTML spans **at PDF generation time only**. The raw `{{...}}` tokens remain in stored HTML so Handlebars can still fill them during future signing rounds.
+
+## Signer Field Structure
+
+Each signer has a `signerFields` JSON column:
+
+```json
+{

codeText:
Subject: docs(e-sign): add spec for PDF placeholder replacement
Body: Made-with: Cursor


Changes:
+# E-Sign PDF Placeholder Replacement
+
+**Date:** 2026-03-24
+**Status:** Approved
+
+## Problem
+
+When generating PDFs from signed record HTML, unfilled signer fields render as raw Handlebars IDs (e.g., `{{79c306e8-bad4-4925-865d-3d12dde3c278_signature_ur1uy}}`). These are ugly and meaningless to end users.
+
+## Solution
+
+Replace unfilled signer field placeholders with styled, colour-coded HTML spans **at PDF generation time only**. The raw `{{...}}` tokens remain in stored HTML so Handlebars can still fill them during future signing rounds.
+
+## Signer Field Structure
+
+Each signer has a `signerFields` JSON column:
+
+```json
+{
+  "colour": { "bg": "#dbeafe", "text": "#1e40af", "border": "#93c5fd" },
+  "fields": [
+    { "id": "r7ncc", "fieldType": "signature", "htmlFieldId": "20031e10-..._signature_r7ncc" },
+    { "id": "gfhk5", "fieldType": "text", "htmlFieldId": "20031e10-..._text_gfhk5" },
+    { "id": "tgsnc", "fieldType": "date", "htmlFieldId": "20031e10-..._date_tgsnc" },
+    { "id": "4vzp6", "fieldType": "initials", "htmlFieldId": "20031e10-..._initials_4vzp6" }
+  ]
+}
+
+```
+
+The `htmlFieldId` pattern is: `{uuid}_{fieldType}_{shortId}`.
+

+# PDF Ad-Hoc Document Signing
+
+Extend the e-sign ad-hoc document flow to support PDF uploads alongside the existing DOCX flow. For PDF, the backend stamps signature images and text onto the PDF at coordinate-based positions using `pdf-lib`, rather than rendering Handlebars placeholders into HTML.
+
+## Design Decisions
+
+| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|
+| Architecture | Approach C: same endpoints, dedicated `PdfDocumentService` | No endpoint duplication, no business logic duplication, clear separation |
+| Signature data format | Base64 PNG image from frontend | Industry standard; frontend already renders with custom font, captures result |
+| Text field data format | Plain string | Backend writes text onto PDF with standard font via `pdf-lib` |
+| PDF delivery to signer | Pre-signed S3 URL from immutable bucket | Matches existing S3 pattern, avoids backend bandwidth |
+| Placeholder storage | Per-recipient in `recipientFields` / per-signer in `signerFields` | NOT on template `genericFieldsPosition`. Each signer only sees their own fields |
+| PDF stamping | Synchronous (not SQS) | `pdf-lib` operates in-memory in milliseconds. YAGNI for async |

diff:
diff --git a/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-02-esign-pdf-snapshot-queue-design.md b/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-02-esign-pdf-snapshot-queue-design.md

--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-02-esign-pdf-snapshot-queue-design.md
@@ -0,0 +1,606 @@
+# E-Sign: Pre-Generate PDF Snapshots via Queue
+
+## Overview
+
+Replace on-demand HTML-to-PDF conversion in the e-sign signed-record download flow with pre-generated immutable PDF snapshots.
+
+For HTML-based e-sign documents:
+
+- generate an immutable PDF for the initial document snapshot
+- generate an immutable PDF for every signature-event snapshot
+- queue PDF generation asynchronously via SQS
+- store PDF artifact state in `metaData` on the owning row
+- stop falling back to on-demand conversion during reads
+
+Native PDF source documents keep the existing direct-PDF behavior and do not use this snapshot pipeline.
+
+## Design Decisions
+
+| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
+|---|---|---|
+| Trigger point | When immutable HTML snapshot is written | PDF should be derived from the persisted source snapshot, not generated on read |
+| Queue transport | SQS | Reuses the repository's existing background-jobs infrastructure |
+| Infra management | CDK-managed dedicated queue + DLQ | Keeps queue provisioning versioned and environment-aware |
+| Reliability model | Direct SQS send after commit + SQS-native retries | SQS redrive handles retries; DLQ catches terminal failures |

+# E-Sign: Void Signed Records
+
+## Summary
+
+Add the ability to void signed records that are in `SENT` or `PARTIALLY_SIGNED` status. Voiding a record makes it permanently inactive — signers can no longer view or sign via their token links, and all pending notifications (reminders, signing requests) are suppressed.
+
+## Decisions
+
+| Decision | Answer |
+|----------|--------|
+| Who can void | Any authenticated user (no CASL — same as templates controller pattern) |
+| Voidable statuses | `SENT` and `PARTIALLY_SIGNED` |
+| Notify signers on void | No — silent void; token validation blocks access |
+| Void reason | Optional `voidReason` string stored on record and in audit trail |
+| Token view/sign on voided record | HTTP 410 `GoneException` with message "This document has been voided" |
+| Disable notifications for voided | Yes — `ESignNotificationHandler` skips voided records |
+| Implementation approach | Dedicated `VoidService` inside `contract-signers` module |
+| Testing approach | TDD — tests written first, watched to fail, then minimal implementation |
+
+## Schema Changes
+
+### Prisma Enum: `AuditEventType`
+
+Add `VOIDED` value to the existing enum.
+

+

+
+## Environments
+
+This CDK app supports:
+

+- `test`
+- `stage`
+- `production`

+

+1. `contract-expiry-daily-<env>`

+   - Payload: `{ "type": "SIGNING_REMINDER_DAILY_CHECK" }`

+

+# Microsoft Authentication — Implementation Plan
+
+> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.
+
+**Goal:** Add `POST /v1/auth/microsoft` endpoint that verifies a Microsoft ID token, looks up the user, and returns a signed challenge JWT for Cognito Custom Auth flow. Also create the Lambda function for the Cognito triggers.
+
+**Architecture:** FE sends MS ID token → BE verifies via JWKS, looks up user in DB + Cognito, signs a short-lived JWT → FE uses JWT as challenge response in Cognito Custom Auth flow → Lambda verifies JWT signature. +One-time (re-runnable) cleanup that deletes `verify.ClientVendorConnection` rows
+that are **not backed by any keep-set source**. Rows created solely from contract
+or MSA events — the two sources now removed from the runtime and backfill — are
+the primary targets, but the script also catches any other degenerate rows
+(null-vendor rows, connections from sources that were later removed, etc.).
+
+## Keep-set (rows in this set are NEVER deleted)
+
+| # | Source | Table(s) | Condition |
+|---|--------|----------|-----------|
+| 1 | **Invited** | `verify.ClientVendorConnection` itself | `verifyVendorId IS NOT NULL` OR `invitationId IS NOT NULL` (any status) |

+| 4 | **Draft (onboarded)** | `public.Vendors` | `createdByClientId = clientId` AND `vendorRegistrationType = 'CLIENT_ONBOARDED'` |

+A connection row is an **orphan** if and only if it satisfies NONE of the four
+keep-set conditions above.

subject: feat(authentication): add cross-tab session sync for login and logout
body:
When a user has the app open in multiple browser tabs, logging out in
one tab left the others on authenticated pages until a manual reload
or an API call detected the expired session. Similarly, logging in on
one tab did not update other tabs sitting on the login page.

Introduce a BroadcastChannel-based sync mechanism that notifies all
same-origin tabs in real time when the auth state changes:

- LOGOUT: receiving tabs delegate to the existing logoutSession flow
  (clear storage, reset Redux/React Query, navigate to /login). The
  Amplify signOut call uses local-only mode on receiving tabs since
  the initiating tab already revoked tokens globally. A re-broadcast
  guard (isBroadcastLogout) prevents echo loops between tabs.

- LOGIN: receiving tabs verify they are not already authenticated and
  that a valid token exists in shared storage before reloading, which
  lets useInitAuthSession bootstrap the session naturally.

- Axios 401 interceptor: forced logouts triggered by token refresh
  failure now also broadcast, so sibling tabs are notified when any
  tab's API call causes a session termination.

Files changed:
- New: useAuthBroadcast.ts (channel, broadcasters, listener hook)
- Modified: useAuth.ts (broadcast on logout, inner try/catch for signOut)
- Modified: AuthRedirectHandler.tsx (mount listener, broadcast on MS SSO)
- Modified: LoginForm.tsx (broadcast on email/password login)
- Modified: config.ts (broadcast on 401-forced logout)
- Modified: hooks/index.ts (re-export new module)

subject: feat(esign): add Stage 2 recipient-specific placeholder fields in template editor
body:
Introduce a two-stage template editing workflow. Stage 1 retains the
existing standard field editing. Stage 2 adds per-recipient placeholder
fields (Signature, Text, Date) with color-coded chips, a recipient
selector dropdown, and recipient field extraction for the save payload.

Key changes:
- Refactor TemplateEditorPage into a directory module with dedicated
  utility hooks (useTemplateEditorStage) for stage-aware logic
- Add recipientColors utility with a 10-colour palette, colour
  assignment by index, and unique field ID generation
- Extend PlaceholderFieldExtension with recipientId, recipientColor,
  and fieldUniqueId attributes; inject CSS custom properties for
  per-recipient chip styling
- Enhance FieldsSidebar with a recipients mode: SearchSelect dropdown,
  selected-recipient badge, and colour-accented drag handles
- Update preprocessHtml to parse recipient placeholder patterns
  ({{recipientId_fieldType_uniqueId}}) and add extractRecipientFields
  for building the recipientFieldsUpdates save payload
- Extend API types with RecipientFieldUpdate, currentStep, and rfp
  metadata on ESignTemplate
- Replace refetchOnMount with staleTime/gcTime: 0 in query hook for
  fresher data on navigation

+## Core Rules
+
+# This is not applicable for inline edit with `ctrl + k`
+
+You have two modes of operation:
+
+1. Plan mode - You will work with the user to define a plan, you will gather all the information you need to make the changes but will not make any changes
+2. Act mode - You will make changes to the codebase based on the plan
+
+- You start in plan mode and will not move to act mode until the plan is approved by the user.
+- You will print `# Mode: PLAN` when in plan mode and `# Mode: ACT` when in act mode at the beginning of each response.
+- Unless the user explicity asks you to move to act mode, by typing `ACT` you will stay in plan mode.
+- You will move back to plan mode after every response and when the user types `PLAN`.
+- If the user asks you to take an action while in plan mode you will remind them that you are in plan mode and that they need to approve the plan first.
+- When in plan mode always output the full updated plan in every response.

refactor(authentication): centralize session init and harden route guards
body:
Run session initialization once from AuthRedirectHandler and keep
isAuthenticating in Redux so useAuth stays a state reader without
duplicate profile/API work on load.

Fix Navigate when the first nav item is missing (fallback to
unauthorized) and group permission checks so explicit allow does not
short-circuit module checks incorrectly.

Replace magic sessionStorage keys with storageKeys, use routeUrls.SIGN
for /sign paths, and align post-login redirect storage with
POST_LOGIN_REDIRECT.

Add ROUTING_AUTH_IMPROVEMENT_PLAN.md to track remaining routing and
auth cleanup.

subject: fix(contract-signing): allow empty table removal and fix Remirror template editor styling
body:
- Add EmptyTableDeleteExtension so Backspace/Delete removes a table when every
  cell is empty. ProseMirror normally only clears cell content and never
  deletes the table node; this extension fills that gap.
- Add Remirror extensions for full HTML fidelity: StrikeExtension (s/del/strike),
  SubExtension, SupExtension, NodeFormattingExtension (align/indent/line-height),
  CodeExtension, CodeBlockExtension. Without these, ProseMirror strips those
  elements on parse and they are lost on save.
- In remirrorHtml.style.css, override Tailwind Preflight so semantic elements
  render correctly: per-level heading sizes (h1–h6), list-style for ul/ol and
  nested ol (lower-alpha/lower-roman), table header (th) bold + background,
  caption, strikethrough, mark/highlight, inline code and pre/code blocks, links,
  hr, sub/sup. Previously headings and other tags appeared uniform or missing.

Fixes CX-3032

+# Design: Move Division from CompliancesProperty to ClientProperties
+
+**Date:** 2026-06-23  
+**Module:** Property Insurance, Properties  
+**Approach:** Division becomes a property-level attribute on ClientProperties; property insurance reads it via the matchedProperty join
+
+---
+
+## Overview
+
+Three coordinated changes across the Properties and Property Insurance modules:
+
+1. **Move `division` field** — remove from `CompliancesProperty`, add to `ClientProperties`
+2. **Property Insurance module cleanup** — remove all division writes; update reads to join `ClientProperties` for division and `externalPropertyId`
+3. **Properties module enhancement** — add division to create, update, list, get, export, and CSV upload APIs
+
+**Key decision:** Division belongs to the property, not the insurance compliance record. Unmatched policies will not have a division. No data migration — existing `CompliancesProperty.division` values are dropped.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Database Schema Changes
+
+### Modified model: `ClientProperties`
+
+Add nullable field after `externalPropertyId`:
+
+```prisma
+division String?
+```
+
+### Modified model: `CompliancesProperty`
+
+Remove field:
+
+```prisma
+// REMOVE: division String?
+```
+
+### Migration
+
+- Add `division`

+# SideNav Child Items UX Refactor
+
+## Summary
+
+Unified the child navigation item behavior between collapsed and expanded sidebar states. Previously, collapsed mode used a **Popover flyout** for child items while expanded mode used an **inline accordion**. Now both modes use the same accordion-based expansion with consistent alignment and proper scrolling.
+
+---
+
+## Problem Statement
+
+The SideNav had two completely different UX patterns for displaying child navigation items depending on whether the sidebar was collapsed or expanded:
+
+| Aspect | Expanded (before) | Collapsed (before) |
+|--------|-------------------|-------------------|
+| Child reveal | Inline accordion below parent | Popover flyout to the right |
+| Interaction | Click toggles accordion | Hover = tooltip, Click = popover |
+| Expansion state | Persisted in `expandedNav` | Not persisted (popover closes on blur) |
+| Visual consistency | Standard nav pattern | Completely different component |
+
+This caused:
+- **Inconsistent UX** — users had to learn two interaction models
+- **State loss** — toggling sidebar collapsed/expanded lost the user's expansion context
+- **No visual hierarchy in collapsed mode** — parent items with children looked identical to regular items
+- **Tooltip + Popover conflicts** — both were bound to the sam

+# Connexus RFP Performance Test Project
+
+This project contains a k6 performance test for the Connexus RFP flow:
+
+```text
+login
+  -> create RFP with many properties
+  -> create selected vendor drafts in chunks
+  -> preview vendor draft summary
+  -> send RFP mail
+  -> optionally poll recipients
+```
+
+The default test assumes properties and vendors already exist. This keeps the
+test focused on the RFP processing path instead of property/vendor provisioning.
+
+## Why k6
+
+k6 is used instead of JMeter because the RFP flow is a chained API workflow with
+large dynamic payloads. JavaScript makes the flow easier to maintain, parameterize,
+and run in CI or containers.
+

+
+```text
+src/rfp-end-to-end.test.js   Main k6 scenario.
+src/config.js                Environment variable parsing.
+src/http-client.js           Shared HTTP wrapper and checks.
+src/auth.js                  /auth/login helper.
+src/payload-builders.js      RFP, vendor draft, optional setup payloads.
+src/extractors.js            Defensive response ID/token extraction helpers.
+data/*.sample.*              Example input files.
+```
+

+
+Create real data files before running a large test:
+
+```text
+data/property-ids.csv
+data/vendor-tenants.csv
+```
